procedure.description: revascularization of the femoral-popliteal artery with atherectomy and stent placement

denial.carcText: The diagnosis is inconsistent with the procedure.
denial.text: Saltmarsh Benefits Administrators denied the claim for CPT 37227 (revascularization of the femoral-popliteal artery with atherectomy and stent placement) with date of service 2026-08-02. CARC 11: The diagnosis is inconsistent with the procedure. Payer remark: The diagnosis reported does not support the procedure billed.

criteria.text: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (ischemic rest pain, non-healing ulcer, or gangrene, Rutherford 4 to 6); or lifestyle-limiting claudication (Rutherford 3) that has failed at least 12 weeks of supervised exercise therapy and optimal medical therapy.
Hemodynamic confirmation: ankle-brachial index 0.4 or less, toe pressure below 30 mmHg, or TcPO2 below 30 mmHg for limb-threatening ischemia (ankle-brachial index below 0.9 for claudication).
Imaging (duplex, CT angiography, or angiography) demonstrating a femoropopliteal stenosis of 50 percent or more, or an occlusion, amenable to endovascular treatment.
Optimal medical therapy documented: an antiplatelet agent, a statin, and smoking cessation or cessation counseling.

chart.text: Here with a cough and congestion for 9 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Blood pressure check. 132 over 77 today, 134 over 91 on repeat. He has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 12 weeks.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 3.3, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 100. Repeat in a year.
He called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Left heel ulcer 2.0 by 1.5 centimeters, pale base, no granulation tissue after 10 weeks of weekly debridement and offloading. Pedal pulses not palpable.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

Called his with the cholesterol results. Total 227, LDL 134, HDL 56, triglycerides 109. Discussed diet and walking. He wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.

70 year old man referred by podiatry for the left leg. Diabetic 16 years, hypertension, prior cataract surgery. Discussed endovascular versus bypass; endovascular first given the anatomy. His history otherwise: anxiety, sees a counselor, migraines, rare now, mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year. Allergies: no drug allergies. Never smoked, occasional beer, lives alone. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Left heel ulcer for 3 months that will not heal despite offloading and weekly wound care, and rest pain in the left foot at night relieved by hanging it off the bed. Rutherford 5. On aspirin 81 and atorvastatin 80. Quit smoking 7 weeks ago after 30 years; counseled again today and offered nicotine replacement.
Arterial studies. Ankle-brachial index left 0.38, right 0.93. Left toe pressure 18 mmHg. Monophasic waveforms at the left popliteal and tibial levels.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 17 and 19. No ocular pathology noted.

CT angiography with runoff: left superficial femoral artery occluded over 12 centimeters from the mid thigh to the adductor canal, reconstitution of the above-knee popliteal artery, two-vessel runoff via the anterior tibial and peroneal. Contralateral mild disease. Aortoiliac segments patent.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 2 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.

Back to review the imaging. Plan left superficial femoral artery recanalization with atherectomy and stent, outpatient. Risks reviewed including embolization and need for bypass. Vitals today 119 over 83, pulse 86.

Mole on the upper back that his spouse noticed. About 6 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change he is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, he will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 10 years.
Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Vitamin D came back 18. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. He mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Pre-procedure visit. Creatinine 1.3, hold metformin, hydration protocol. Consent signed.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 11 denial can be answered from the record.
